entries.name: James Glasgow
entries.argument: The live biographies identify two distinct adult Larne men: James Glasgow-1509, ropemaker (1737–1802), and James Glasgow-3991, probable tanner (about 1748–1812). Both survived until the 1779 lease. The separate 1768 messuage names a ropemaker party and a farmer witness, whose roles require separate comparison. Glasgow-1509 is the leading compatible party. No source names the farmer witness's relatives or identifies the 1779 lessee. The 1832 renewal does not establish Anne or Jane as James’s daughters. Keep the 1768 ropemaker party, farmer witness and 1779 lessee roles separate. Jane, wife of Glasgow-3991, died in 1820 and cannot be the 1832 lessee.
entries.integration_recommendation: Separate the 1768 party and witness roles from the 1779 lessee assessment. Retain Glasgow-1509 and Glasgow-3991 as candidates for 1779. Title succession alone does not prove the women were daughters.

candidate_public_evidence.bio_evidence:
[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]]

== Biography ==
'''James Glasgow''' was reportedly born in '''1737'''. A Larne or Kilwaughter congregational record is said to contain an entry for a James, son of [[Glasgow-1499|Hugh Glasgow]], at '''New Town, Larne''', in that year.

The original congregational entry, or a reliable full transcription, has not yet been cited on this profile. The exact birth date, place and identification of Hugh as James’s father should therefore be treated as probable rather than conclusively established.

James was a '''ropemaker''' at Larne, County Antrim. A lease dated 10 September 1760, registered on 24 November 1763, describes him as a ropemaker of Belfast and leases him a marked-out ropewalk at Gardenmore in Larne for thirty-one years from 1 November 1760. He agreed to build a house at the south end of the ropewalk.<ref name="Ropewalk1760">Registry of Deeds transcript, lease dated 10 September 1760 and registered 24 November 1763, [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSH3-S7XZ-8 FamilySearch image].</ref>

On 28 March 1768 James, described as a ropemaker of the Old Town of Larne, assigned the plot, workhouse and remainder of the same lease to John Hill for £50. The matching commencement date and rent identify it as the 1760 ropewalk.<ref name=

[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]]
== Biography ==

'''James Glasgow''' was born about 1748, the son of '''[[Glasgow-1499|Hugh Glasgow]]''' and his wife '''[[Unknown-763010|Ann Glasgow]]'''. His approximate year of birth is calculated from his age at death.<ref name="Armorial">"Armorial Sculptured Stones of the County Antrim," ''Ulster Journal of Archaeology'', second series 6 (1900), [https://archive.org/details/ulsterjournalofa06ulstiala/page/47/mode/1up p. 47], Glasgow monument inscription.</ref>

The family monument explicitly identifies James as the son of Hugh and Ann Glasgow. Hugh died on 8 July 1767, aged 62, and Ann died on 8 June 1786, aged 75.<ref name="Armorial" />

James married '''[[Unknown-763421|Jane]]''', whose maiden name is not given in the monument inscription. Jane was born about 1741, based on her recorded age at death.<ref name="Armorial" />

James and Jane had at least one known child:

* '''[[Glasgow-3992|Ann Glasgow]]''', born about 1768; died 25 May 1832, aged 64.<ref name="Armorial" />

James died on '''14 April 1812''', aged 64.<ref name="Armorial" /> His stated age places his birth approximately between 15 April 1747 and 14 April 1748.

His wife Jane survived him. She died on '''21 July 1820''', aged 79.<ref name="Armorial" />

=== Tanner at Larne ===

== Biography ==

An 1874 indenture traces James Glasgow’s 2 October 1779 Newtown of Larne lease to a 25 February 1832 renewal to Anne and Jane Glasgow.<ref>Inspected historical source; https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CS54-77Q4-H; . Original recital inspected. It establishes title succession, not stated descent; James and both women’s identities remain unresolved.</ref>

The separate memorial 173108 records James Glasgow, ropemaker, assigning a messuage to John Hill on 28 March 1768; its witnessing James Glasgow is described as farmer.<ref>Inspected historical source; https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSJW-DDD6; ; Inspected historical source; https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSJW-DDDL; . Original occupation checked. The same-day ropewalk and messuage assignments are different instruments. Whether the farmer and tanner witnesses are one man is unresolved.</ref>

== Research Notes ==

The live biographies identify two distinct adult Larne men: James Glasgow-1509, ropemaker (1737–1802), and James Glasgow-3991, probable tanner (about 1748–1812). Both survived until the 1779 lease. The separate 1768 messuage names a ropemaker party and a farmer witness, whose roles require separate comparison. Glasgow-1509 is the leading compatible party. No source names the farmer witness's relatives or identifies the 1779 lessee. The 1832 renewal does not establish Anne or Jane as James’s daughters. Keep the 1768 ropemaker party, farmer witness and 1779 lessee roles separate. Jane, wife of Glasgow-3991, died in 1820 and cannot be the 1832 lessee.

Possible profile identities: [[Glasgow-1509]], [[Glasgow-3991]].

Next research: Inspect the named original record and compare dated family evidence; retained candidates remain unproved.

entries.name: Thomas Ross
entries.argument: The original 1901 Gortereghy return describes Thomas Ross, 34, as farmer and flax miller, with Scotland-born wife Mary Jane and children. This strongly supports the 1912 mill-owner occurrence. The 1911 household reports 24 years of marriage. Ross-13124 remains compatible, with differing reported census ages. Ross-29596 has severe chronology tension if his cited 1874 birth is correct: he would be about 12 at marriage and 11 when Jeannie was born. The birth image returned HTTP 403, so this remains a conditional conflict rather than a fresh original-based exclusion. The 1912 Belfast and Ulster Directory lists Thomas Ross as a mill owner at Gortreighy in the neighbourhood inhabitants section for Rasharkin. It adds a named economic and geographic associate in the townland where the Glasgow family lived in the earlier baptism period, but it does not establish any relationship to Alexander Glasgow or the McCaughan/Elder families.<ref>1912 Belfast and Ulster Directory, Rasharkin; https://lennonwylie.co.uk/PT191214.htm; . Ross-13124 remains compatible; the reported census ages differ.<ref>1901 Gortereghy, Thomas Ross household; https://api-census.nationalarchives.ie/census/image/nai000298459.pdf; Form A; printed house 38; rows 1–8; 1911 Gortereghy, Thomas Ross household; https://api-census.nationalarchives.ie/census/image/nai001390150.pdf; Form A; official index house 34; rows 1–8. Ross-29596 has severe chronology tension if his cited 1874 birth is correct: he would be about 12 at marriage and 11 when Jeannie was born. This is a new direct memorial transcription for the catalogue's parentage study, not a Glasgow record and not proof that the Elder family was related to Alexander Glasgow. The memorial supplies a named Elder household for future comparison with the later Robert Elder who occupied Alexander Glasgow's former Lisnagaver lot; identity between those Elder references remains unproved.</ref>

Alexander married Mary Anderson, full-age spinster of Gortreaghy, daughter of Neil Anderson; witnesses were Robert Anderson and Margaret Elder.<ref>RootsChat, Elder, Murdoch & McMeekin Families; https://www.rootschat.com/forum/index.php?topic=214109.0; . The entry is not yet an inspected original, so it is a secondary-source lead rather than final evidence. It is nevertheless a new, specific parent-bearing record for the Gortreaghy Elder household and gives a testable route for determining whether the Alexander Elder on the Rasharkin Second Presbyterian memorial was a son of the Robert Elder who later occupied Alexander Glasgow's Lisnagaver lot. That identity chain remains unproved.</ref>

== Biography ==

'''Ann or Anne Glasgow''' was born about 1847 in County Antrim, Ireland. She was the daughter of [[Glasgow-951|Alexander Glasgow]] and [[McCaughan-222|Mary McCaughan]].

In 1851 she was recorded as their four-year-old daughter in the family household at Lisnagaver, Rasharkin parish, County Antrim.<ref name="Census1851">[https://www.census.nationalarchives.ie/pages/1851/Antrim/Kilconway/Rasharkin/Lisnagaver/35/ National Archives of Ireland, 1851 census], Alexander Glasgow household, Lisnagaver, house 35.</ref>

On 13 October 1876 Ann married '''Robert McCracken''' at Ballymoney. The register describes Robert as a full-age bachelor and farmer of Lisnagaver, son of William McCracken, labourer. Ann was a full-age spinster of Lisnagaver and named her father as Alexander Glasgow, labourer. Samuel Taylor and Mary Ann Henry witnessed the marriage.<ref name="Marriage1876">General Register Office of Ireland, civil marriage register, Robert McCracken and Ann Glasgow, 13 October 1876; [https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/files/civil/marriage_returns/marriages_1876/11181/8097170.pdf digital image].</ref>

Their known child, [[McCracken-5690|William James McCracken]], was born at Lisnagaver on 21 September 1877.

entries.argument: McCaw-443, born about 1818 in Londonderry and later a Presbyterian minister with Sarah in 1861, and McCaw-216, born in 1821 in Ireland and married to Elizabeth Jane Werden about 1845 in Canada, could chronologically have fathered a child in 1839. == Biography ==

A fresh audit of the surviving Rasharkin Presbyterian baptism transcription located a second parent-bearing McCaughern/Macaw household at the target townland. Hugh Macaw was born 3 February 1839 and baptised 3 March 1839 as the son of William and Mary Kilpatrick, resident at Lisnagaver (entry 125).<ref>Rasharkin Presbyterian baptisms, entries 125 and 204; https://genealogy.torrens.org/BannValley/church/RasharkinP/Baptisms_1834.html; . The same register records Jane Matilda Macaw, born 26 July 1843 and baptised 14 January 1844, as the daughter of William and Mary Kilpatrick at Granagh (entry 204). Named transcription reread 30 September 2026; originalmanuscriptuninspected.</ref>

Rereading Rasharkin baptism transcription entry 125 gives Hugh Macaw’s birth as 3 February 1839, replacing the maintained 5 February wording. His baptism remains 3 March 1839; original manuscript inspection is required before treating the corrected transcription as a final date.<ref>Rasharkin Presbyterian baptism transcription; https://genealogy.torrens.org/BannValley/church/RasharkinP/Baptisms_1834.html; transcription entries 125 and 204; original MIC/1P/292 uninspected. Named transcription reread; original manuscript uninspected.</ref>

== Research Notes ==

McCaw-443, born about 1818 in Londonderry and later a Presbyterian minister with Sarah in 1861, and McCaw-216, born in 1821 in Ireland and married to Elizabeth Jane Werden about 1845 in Canada, could chronologically have fathered a child in 1839. A later different wife is not an exclusion without continuous marriage evidence. Both are weak comparisons, without a Lisnagaver connection to named wife Mary Kilpatrick. The Antrim Williams born in 1840 and 1865 cannot be the 1839 father. Consolidate Hugh and Jane Matilda with the same named parental couple. Rereading the transcription gives 3 February 1839, with the manuscript still uninspected. Parent profile identities remain uncertain; later spouses alone do not exclude an earlier family.

Possible profile identities: [[McCaw-443]], [[McCaw-216]].

Next research: Inspect the named original record and compare dated family evidence; retained candidates remain unproved.

entries.argument: Kilpatrick-3023 represents Mary, born about 1820 and died in 1870, associated with Larne/Antrim. Consolidate Hugh and Jane Matilda with the same named parental couple. Rereading the transcription gives 3 February 1839, with the manuscript still uninspected. Parent profile identities remain uncertain; later spouses alone do not exclude an earlier family.

entries.name: Joseph Elder
entries.argument: No supported existing Joseph profile was identified for the Gortereghy man aged 79 in 1911. Elder-3002 has a nearby birth year of 1831 but documents an Alabama marriage in 1852, Civil War service and burial in Clay County in 1913, without an Irish household chain. Elder-741 is an undated, unlocated import retained only as a name-only lead. Robert Elder-7144's biography mentions brother Joseph leasing Gortereghy land in 1864, an important compatible earlier record without a Joseph profile ID.
entries.integration_recommendation: Keep one Joseph draft combining the 1911 record with comparison to the probable 1864 lessee. Identify Robert Elder-7144 as a possible brother; the uninspected original 1911 form does not prove that relationship.

== Biography ==

'''Sarah (Dysart) McCaughern''' — recorded as '''Sallie''' — was a daughter of [[Dysart-1684|James Dysart]] and [[Glasglow-11|Jane Catherine (Glasgow) Dysart]] of Crushybracken, Rasharkin parish, County Antrim. She was a minor when she married [[McCaughern-23|John McCaughern]] of Gortereghy at Rasharkin Presbyterian Church on 18 March 1851.

Her daughter [[McCaughern-24|Mary Anne McCaughern]] was named residuary legatee in the 1881 will of her grandfather James Dysart. Sarah is the "Sallie, daughter of Jane Dysart, residing at Ballymena" of the 14 January 1892 probate citation of [[Glasgow-4070|Nancy Glasgow]].

== Biography ==

A fresh audit of the surviving Rasharkin Presbyterian baptism transcription located a second parent-bearing McCaughern/Macaw household at the target townland. Hugh Macaw was born 3 February 1839 and baptised 3 March 1839 as the son of William and Mary Kilpatrick, resident at Lisnagaver (entry 125).<ref>Rasharkin Presbyterian baptisms, entries 125 and 204; https://genealogy.torrens.org/BannValley/church/RasharkinP/Baptisms_1834.html; . The same register records Jane Matilda Macaw, born 26 July 1843 and baptised 14 January 1844, as the daughter of William and Mary Kilpatrick at Granagh (entry 204). Named transcription reread 30 September 2026; originalmanuscriptuninspected.</ref>

Rereading Rasharkin baptism transcription entry 125 gives Hugh Macaw’s birth as 3 February 1839, replacing the maintained 5 February wording. His baptism remains 3 March 1839; original manuscript inspection is required before treating the corrected transcription as a final date.<ref>Rasharkin Presbyterian baptism transcription; https://genealogy.torrens.org/BannValley/church/RasharkinP/Baptisms_1834.html; transcription entries 125 and 204; original MIC/1P/292 uninspected. Named transcription reread; original manuscript uninspected.</ref>

== Research Notes ==

No compatible infant profile was identified through Hugh Macaw/McCaw/McCaughan searches. McCaw-10 represents the father of John, born about 1833. McCaw-233 represents an adult born about 1812 and father of Eliza, born about 1832. These are older generations, not the 1839 infant. The freshly inspected published baptism transcription, row 125, gives birth on 3 February 1839 and baptism on 3 March, whereas the maintained handoff gave 5 February. The original image is still needed to settle the date. Consolidate Hugh and Jane Matilda with the same named parental couple. Rereading the transcription gives 3 February 1839, with the manuscript still uninspected. Parent profile identities remain uncertain; later spouses alone do not exclude an earlier family.

Possible profile identities: none established within the recorded searches.

Next research: Inspect the named original record and compare dated family evidence; retained candidates remain unproved.

It confirms a substantial McCaughern household in the same townland as the Elder and Glasgow-associated records, but it does not identify Sarah's husband, parents or relationship to Mary Glasgow.<ref>1911 Gortereghy, Sarah McCaughern household; https://api-census.nationalarchives.ie/census/image/nai001390134.pdf; Form A; official index house 26; rows 1–6. The original 1901 and 1911 returns establish continuity of Sarah McCaughern’s Gortereghy family. Sarah was a Derry-born widow aged 72/82; Caroline, Sarah J/Sara Jane, James A/Jas Alex, Matilda and grandson George occur in both returns. Elizabeth, 32, is also a daughter in 1901. Sarah Dysart-1893, married in 1851 to Gortereghy farmer John McCaughern, remains the strongest mother identity, but neither census names her deceased husband or maiden surname.<ref>1901 Gortereghy, Sarah McCaughern household; https://api-census.nationalarchives.ie/census/image/nai000298441.pdf; Form A; official index house 18; rows 1–7; 1911 Gortereghy, Sarah McCaughern household; https://api-census.nationalarchives.ie/census/image/nai001390134.pdf; Form A; official index house 26; rows 1–6; Rasharkin Presbyterian civil marriage register 1851; https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/files/civil/marriage_returns/marriages_1851/09402/5405894.pdf; PDF page 1; entry 28.
